thread:
taylor: FYI — consolidated follow-ups from the cross-region routing + LB retries postmortem. Putting owners & timelines here so nothing drifts. PTAL and add if I missed anything. https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/PM-4321

raj: Thanks. Quick Q — is the DNS TTL mitigation still in place for regions that flapped?

morgan: Yes, we extended the low-TTL rollback for us-west and eu-west at 02:15 UTC and reverted to 60s last night after stability check. Leaving records updated until next Friday as a precaution.

laura: Taking ownership of the routing rule audit. I'll run sweep for mis-typed SNI fallback rules and duplicate LB weights. ETA EOD Thu.

sam: Noted. I have a PR that enforces stricter LB weight validation in the infra config CI: orch/PR-4567. It rejects configs where weight_sum != 100 for multi-backend LB entries. Target merge tomorrow morning.

raj: Awesome. Are we sure the retry storm originates from client-side retry + cross-region failover combo? I saw a pattern where clients retried on connection_reset and ended up hitting a secondary region which also had transient 503s.

morgan: Correct. Logs show ~70% of retries were triggered by connection reset within 300ms of initial attempt. Once the client retried, smart-routing pushed to fallback region and the load spike amplified. Extract from logs: 
```
[2026-06-12T01:04:23Z] conn_reset upstream=lb-us-west-2 seq=3421 route=primary -> fallback
[2026-06-12T01:04:23Z] upstream_503 count=18 backlog=120
```

laura: Two remediation threads from the postmortem I think: (A) Prevent amplification (client-facing mitigations / retry budget guidance) and (B) Fix routing correctness (LB rules + TLS SNI handling).

sam: For (A) we should publish a short SDK guidance note: recommended retry/backoff and when to use hedged requests. I'll draft and aim to publish by next Tue. Owner: sam.

laura: For (B) I'll do the routing sweep + add unit test coverage for SNI->route mapping. If I hit ambiguous configs, I'll open a config-cleanup ticket and tag platform.

taylor: Great. I'll coordinate the rollout plan for the LB validation PR so we can gate on dedicated canaries first. Proposed plan: merge -> canary to staging -> 2-hour observation -> promote to prod for one region -> 24h observation -> full rollout. Scheduler: start canaries Tue 06:00 UTC if PR merged Mon night.

raj: Also propose an automatic temporary throttling policy when LB error rates exceed threshold: limit per-origin concurrent new connections for 10 min then gradually relax. That will curb cascade. Owner: raj, prototype by next Fri.

morgan: Created alert: incidents:lb-retry-amplification with threshold 5x baseline sustained 3m. SRE-bot hooked it to the oncall rotation.

sre-bot: alert created (id: alert-89321) -> notify @oncall on triggers.

taylor: Action items summary (I'll paste into the postmortem follow-up doc):
- laura: routing rule & SNI sweep; tests; open cleanup tickets if needed — ETA Thu EOD
- sam: infra CI LB-weight validation PR (orch/PR-4567) — target merge Mon morning
- sam: SDK retry guidance doc — draft by Tue
- raj: throttling prototype to limit new concurrent connections on spike — prototype by Fri
- morgan: keep TTL mitigation until next Fri and monitor; oncall to escalate if alert fires — ongoing
- taylor: coordinate canary rollout + observe windows; update postmortem doc with dates once PR merged — follow-up next Wed

taylor: Can everyone react with :thumbsup: when they confirm the ownership and ETA, or reply if dates need adjusting. I'll set a recurring weekly check-in for the next 4 weeks to watch for recurrence patterns.

laura: :thumbsup: — will update ticket with progress comments.

sam: :thumbsup: — will push CI change tomorrow AM.

raj: :thumbsup: — Fri prototype might slip one day if infra capacity blocked, but will update if that happens.

morgan: :thumbsup: — monitoring dashboards updated, will post a short snapshot in #incidents daily for the week.

taylor: Thanks all. If we see the retry amplification again, escalate to postmortem immediately and consider temporary global traffic-shaping.

raj: Also, can we add a retro note: investigate whether TLS handshake failures correlated with a cert rotation window earlier that day. I saw a small spike around cert-check job at 00:50 UTC.

laura: I'll correlate cert rotations with the routing logs during my sweep. If it's coupled, we'll add a pre-check in the cert rotation job that verifies active route stability before mass rollouts.

morgan: Saved. I'll attach the relevant logs to PM-4321 and mark them as evidence for the timeline.

sre-bot: reminder scheduled: follow-up check-in in 7 days for PM-4321.

taylor: Closing thread here — thanks everyone. I'll update the postmortem doc with this action table and ping for any changes.
